Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:

– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The bug report states that the TarArchiveInputStream silently finishes when an unexpected EOF occurs instead of throwing an IOException, which contradicts the previous behavior expected by the test case shouldThrowAnExceptionOnTruncatedEntries.

From analyzing the test code, it expects an IOException during reading entries from a deliberately truncated tar file (indicating a corrupt archive). The test iterates through entries with getNextTarEntry() and copies data until no more entries.

In the implementation of TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry():
- It first skips any remaining data from the current entry (skip(Long.MAX_VALUE)) and any record padding (skipRecordPadding()).
- Then it calls getRecord() to read the next tar header block.
- getRecord() calls readRecord() which reads a full fixed-size record from the input stream with IOUtils.readFully().
- readRecord() returns null if less than a full record could be read (which indicates EOF or truncated input).
- If getRecord() sees an EOF record (all zeroes) or null, it sets hasHitEOF = true and handles consuming any trailing bytes.
- If a null header block is returned, getNextTarEntry() returns null indicating no more entries.
- Importantly, no explicit IOException is thrown if a truncated record is read (readRecord() returns null). Instead, getNextTarEntry() simply returns null, signaling EOF.
- The skip() method invoked earlier in getNextTarEntry() only skips to the end of the current entry size without throwing exceptions on premature stream truncation.
- There are other parts of getNextTarEntry() handling GNU long name/link entries and sparse entries, but they also rely on getRecord() which silently returns null for unexpected EOF instead of failing.

Hence, the core reason the truncated input no longer causes an IOException to be thrown is because the readRecord() method silently returns null on incomplete record reads. This makes getNextTarEntry() interpret incomplete/truncated input as EOF rather than a corrupt archive condition requiring exception throwing, violating the expectations of the test case.

In summary, the root cause is that the method reading the tar header record (readRecord) and by extension getRecord and getNextTarEntry do not detect and fail on unexpected EOF/truncated records, leading to silent completion instead of the previously expected IOException for malformed archives. This mismatch explains the test failure and matches the bug report's problem description.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
